Model 2: Weighted-Normal Niche (Paper Eq. 5/8)

Source: vignettes/model_weighted.Rmd
model_weighted.Rmd

1 Ecological Motivation

The presence-only model (Model 1) ignores the distribution of environments in the accessible area \(M\). When some environments are more common than others, the uncorrected MLE is biased toward those common environments.

The weighted-normal model corrects for this by incorporating a kernel density estimate (KDE) \(\hat{g}(\mathbf{x})\) of the environmental density in \(M\). The weight function \(w(\mathbf{x}) = \hat{g}(\mathbf{x})\) enters both the numerator and denominator of the restricted likelihood, modelling an observation process where the probability of recording a presence at \(\mathbf{x}\) is proportional to the product of the species’ suitability \(f(\mathbf{x})\) and the environmental availability \(g(\mathbf{x})\).

This is the default model in nicher and implements Equation 5 (or equivalently Equation 8 with \(w = \hat{g}\)) of Jimenez and Soberón (2022).

2 Data-Generating Process

The weighted model assumes the use-availability DGP:

\[ p(\mathbf{x}_i \mid \text{presence in } M) = \frac{f(\mathbf{x}_i;\mu,\Sigma)\;\hat{g}(\mathbf{x}_i)} {\int_M f(\mathbf{x};\mu,\Sigma)\;\hat{g}(\mathbf{x})\,d\mathbf{x}}. \tag{1} \]

This assumes that the intensity of presence records at environment \(\mathbf{x}\) is proportional to both the species’ fundamental niche density \(f\) and the environmental density \(g\) in \(M\). This is appropriate when:

  • Observation probability correlates with environmental density (e.g. opportunistic citizen-science records where more observers visit common habitats).
  • The analyst wants to model the realised niche as shaped by both intrinsic tolerances and environmental availability.

3 Mathematical Specification

3.1 Restricted Log-Likelihood (Paper Eq. 5)

\[ \ell(\mu,\Sigma) = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\log f(\mathbf{x}_i) + \sum_{i=1}^{n}\log \hat{g}(\mathbf{x}_i) - n\,\log\!\sum_{j=1}^{K}\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j)\,f(\mathbf{y}_j), \tag{2} \]

where \(\{\mathbf{y}_j\}_{j=1}^K\) are background points sampled from \(M\).

3.2 Negative Log-Likelihood (Minimised Objective)

Dropping the \(\log f\) normalisation constant \((2\pi)^{-p/2}|\Sigma|^{-1/2}\) from the denominator (it cancels between numerator and denominator up to a factor that does not affect the optimum), the minimised objective is:

\[ -\ell^*(\theta) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{n} q_i - \sum_{i=1}^{n}\log\hat{g}(\mathbf{x}_i) + n\cdot\operatorname{logsumexp}_j\!\left[ \log\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j) - \tfrac{1}{2}q_j \right] + \lambda\sum_{k=1}^{p}(\log\sigma_k - c_k)^2, \tag{3} \]

where:

  • \(q_i = \|L^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_i - \mu)\|^2\) is the squared Mahalanobis distance at presence point \(i\),
  • \(q_j = \|L^{-1}(\mathbf{y}_j - \mu)\|^2\) at background point \(j\),
  • \(\hat{g}(\cdot)\) is the Gaussian KDE of the background evaluated at the point,
  • \(c_k = \log\hat\sigma_k(\text{env\_occ})\) centres the ridge prior at the sample standard deviation of each variable,
  • \(\lambda\) controls the ridge strength (default 1.0; set to 0 for pure paper Eq. 5).

3.3 The Ridge Prior

The pure MLE of the weighted-normal model is susceptible to the Patil & Ord (1976) drift: as \(\sigma_k \to \infty\), the numerator density \(f(\mathbf{x}_i)\) flattens, the denominator approaches \(\sum_j \hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j)\) (a constant), and the likelihood increases without bound.

The ridge term \(\lambda\sum_k(\log\sigma_k - c_k)^2\) is a weakly informative prior that penalises log-standard-deviations far from the empirical scale, preventing this drift while having negligible influence near the optimum. Users can set \(\lambda = 0\) to recover the exact paper formula, but this is not recommended for multimodal \(M\).

3.4 Sign Convention (vs. ip_weighted)

Note the signs on the KDE terms:

Term "weighted" (this model) "ip_weighted" (Model 3)
Denominator integrand \(+\log\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j) - \frac{1}{2}q_j\) \(-\frac{1}{2}q_j - \log\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j)\)
Numerator KDE \(-\sum_i\log\hat{g}(\mathbf{x}_i)\) \(+\sum_i\log\hat{g}(\mathbf{x}_i)\)

These sign differences correspond to \(w = \hat{g}\) (weighted) vs. \(w = 1/\hat{g}\) (ip_weighted). Both are instances of Equation 8 with different weight functions.

4 Implementation Call Chain 

optimize_niche(likelihood = "weighted")
  └─ niche_obj.cpp::create_niche_obj_ptr()
       └─ loglik_niche_math_weighted_eigen()       [C++, lines 324–381]
            ├─ build_L_cov()                        [theta → mu, sigma, L_cov]
            ├─ Mahalanobis q1 (occurrences), q2 (background)
            ├─ a_j = log_w_den - 0.5 * q2           [line 366]
            ├─ logsumexp(a)                          [lines 368–370]
            ├─ neg_log = 0.5*sum_q1 - log_w_occ + n*lse + penalty
            └─ prior_penalty_value()                 [ridge on log_sigma]

4.1 Key Code (loglik_niche_math_cpp.cpp, lines 324–381)

The C++ kernel:

  1. Reconstructs \(L_{\text{cov}}\) from \(\theta\) via build_L_cov().
  2. Computes Mahalanobis distances for both presence and background points.
  3. Clamps KDE weights: w.max(MIN_KDE_WEIGHT).log() with MIN_KDE_WEIGHT = 1e-300 to prevent \(\log(0) = -\infty\).
  4. Computes the logsumexp of \(a_j = \log\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j) - \frac{1}{2}q_j\) (line 366).
  5. Adds the ridge penalty via prior_penalty_value() (line 372–373).
  6. Returns the guarded negative log-likelihood (line 379).

4.2 Analytic Gradient (lines 383–499)

The gradient is computed analytically for \(\mu\) and \(\log\sigma\), and by central finite differences for the C-vine partial-correlation block \(v\):

  • \(\nabla_\mu\): Closed-form via \(\Sigma^{-1}[\text{weighted mean shift}]\) (lines 449–457).
  • \(\nabla_{\log\sigma_k}\): Closed-form via \(U \odot V\) products with softmax weights \(\pi_j\) (lines 459–464).
  • \(\nabla_{v_k}\): Central FD with step \(\Delta = |v_k| \cdot h_{\text{rel}} + h_{\text{abs}}\) (lines 466–484).
  • Ridge gradient: Added by prior_penalty_grad_add() (line 493).

4.3 R Entry Point 

optimize_niche(env_occ, env_m, likelihood = "weighted",
               prior_log_sigma_lambda = 1.0)

5 KDE Computation

The background KDE \(\hat{g}\) is computed once before optimisation begins (it depends only on the data, not on \(\theta\)). The KDE uses a Gaussian kernel with Scott’s rule bandwidth:

\[ h_k = \hat\sigma_k \cdot K^{-1/(p+4)}, \]

where \(K\) is the number of reference points and \(\hat\sigma_k\) is the sample standard deviation of the \(k\)-th environmental variable in the background. For \(p = 2\), a specialised kde_2d() kernel is used; for \(p \geq 3\), the general kde_eigen() kernel handles arbitrary dimensions.

6 Analytical Properties

Property Value
MLE for \(\mu\) No closed form (implicit through the weighted denominator)
Likelihood shape Can be multimodal for complex \(M\)
Identifiability Full for finite \(M\) with ridge (\(\lambda > 0\))
Background data Required (\(\mathbf{y}_j\) from \(M\))
KDE weights Precomputed, fixed during optimisation
Regularisation Ridge prior on \(\log\sigma\) (default \(\lambda = 1\))

7 When To Use

  • Default choice for most species distribution modelling workflows.
  • When observation probability correlates with environmental density (opportunistic records, citizen-science data).
  • When the goal is to estimate the niche as observed through M’s lens (realised niche under the use-availability DGP).
  • When \(M\) is unimodal or mildly multimodal (the ridge prior handles moderate non-convexity).

8 Limitations

  1. DGP assumption. Assumes presence intensity \(\propto f \cdot g\). If sampling effort is uniform across \(M\) and the goal is the fundamental niche on Lebesgue measure, consider "ip_weighted" (Model 3) instead.

  2. Patil & Ord drift (without ridge). Setting \(\lambda = 0\) recovers the exact paper Eq. 5 but the MLE may not exist (\(\sigma \to \infty\)). Always use \(\lambda > 0\) in practice.

  3. KDE bandwidth sensitivity. Scott’s rule may over- or under-smooth. Diagnostic plots of \(\hat{g}\) are recommended.

  4. Normality assumption. The niche is ellipsoidal. For asymmetric niches, consider "skew_normal_weighted" (Model 5) or "skew_t_weighted" (Model 7).

References

Jimenez, L., and J. Soberón. 2022. “Weighted Likelihood Estimation of the Fundamental Niche.” Ecological Modelling 470: 110009. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2022.110009.
